sections.title: The letter emme
paragraphs: The letter is called (emme) /ˈɛmme/. Its main sound is heard in (mare) /ˈma.re/, which means sea. This letter has only one sound in standard Italian. You hear it at the start, in the middle, and doubled inside words. It is always steady and clear.

sections.title: Mouth movements
paragraphs: Close both lips gently together to block the mouth. Keep your tongue relaxed and low. Turn your voice on and let the air escape through your nose. Place two fingers on the front of your neck to feel your vocal cords vibrate.

sections.title: Reading the letter
paragraphs: This letter always keeps the same sound in all positions. You hear it as /m/ at the start of a word in (mare) /ˈma.re/. When written twice, hold your closed lips for more time, as in (mamma) /ˈmam.ma/.

sections.title: Common pitfalls
paragraphs: This sound matches the sound in map or summer. Hold your lips firmly closed and keep the sound resonant. There is no real pitfall with this letter in Italian.
